cards.text: Hosea is a prophet, and the word of the LORD came to him (Hosea 1:1). This message is for the people of Israel, and it opens by shutting a celebration down: 'Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations…'

cards.question: Hosea tells Israel not to celebrate like the nations do. Why not?

answers.text: They've been unfaithful to their God
They just lost their king in battle
Their harvest came in far too late

cards.text: Hosea calls it playing the harlot against God, making 'love for hire on every threshing floor.' Keep your eye on those threshing floors, friend, because Hosea's not done with them.

cards.question: True or false: The threshing floor and the winepress will keep feeding Israel.

cards.text: Then it gets heavier: they won't remain in the land of the LORD, and Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, will return to Egypt. Yes, EGYPT, the very place God says He called His son out of (Hosea 11:1).

cards.question: Ephraim is headed back to Egypt. Where else will they end up eating unclean food?

cards.text: They won't pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices won't please Him. Hosea says those sacrifices will be to them 'like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled.'

cards.question: True or false: Hosea says Israel's bread will still go into the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Hosea asks, 'What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?' Picture the biggest baking day of the year, and you're stuck across town with no oven, just standing there holding a bag of chocolate chips.

cards.question: Hosea says even if Israel flees destruction, Egypt will gather them. Which city will bury them?
True or false: Hosea pictures Israel's tents overrun with thorns.

cards.text: Now the alarm sounds: 'The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived…' Hosea says let Israel know it, and friend, there's no snooze button on this one.

cards.question: Israel's iniquity and hostility are so great that the prophet who warns them gets called a ___.

cards.text: And the inspired man? Called insane. That's like yelling 'The oven is SMOKING!' and the whole kitchen says, 'Relax, Dorin, you are being dramatic again.'
The prophet is Ephraim's watchman, along with God. Yet 'the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths.'

cards.question: Then comes a shocking line about where hostility is found. Where is it?

answers.text: In the house of his God
At the gates of the city

cards.text: Hosea says they have 'deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah…' Gibeah is a town, and Hosea doesn't spell out what happened there, but it's nothing good.

cards.question: Hosea says God will remember Israel's ___ and punish their sins.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks: 'I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.' Grapes. In the WILDERNESS. He saw their fathers as the first figs of the season.
But they went to Baal-peor (Baal is a false god) and 'consecrated themselves to Shame…' That's a sharp turn, friend.

cards.question: Israel's fathers gave themselves to Shame at Baal-peor. What did they become?

answers.text: As detestable as what they loved
As strong as the nations around them
As free as birds in the wilderness

cards.text: Next line: 'Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird…' Friend, I've watched birds leave a kitchen windowsill, and they do NOT come back to say goodbye.

cards.question: True or false: As Ephraim's glory flies away like a bird, there will be no births in Ephraim.

cards.text: Even if they raise children, the LORD says He will bereave them of each one. That's a heavy line, friend.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says woe to Ephraim when He turns away from them.

cards.text: The LORD says He has seen Ephraim like Tyre, a rich trading city on the sea (Ezekiel 27:33), planted in a meadow. But Ephraim 'will bring out his children for slaughter.'
Then comes a cry to the LORD: 'Give them, O LORD—what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!'

cards.question: Next the LORD says all of Ephraim's evil appears in one place, and that He hated them there. Where?
Because of their wicked deeds, where will the LORD drive Ephraim from?

cards.text: Then the LORD says it plainly: 'I will no longer love them…'

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says Ephraim's leaders have stayed faithful to Him.

cards.text: Remember the grapes and the first figs? Now the picture is a plant in the ground, and it's in trouble: 'Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered…'

cards.question: Ephraim's root is withered, so they cannot bear ___.

cards.text: And the LORD says that even if they bear children, He will slay 'the darlings of their wombs.'

cards.question: One last line says God will reject Ephraim. Why?
Rejected by God, Ephraim shall be ___ among the nations.
